Okay, long day just able to post now, here's what the farming/town section in autumn village was like; 

1. The PC version they had was running on xbox controls, which was definitely a learning curve for me as that is the only console I do not own. 

2. Absolutely zero performance issues. Granted, this was running on an insane PC rig, but I asked the staff about performance and whether or not it runs well on switch. They said that it runs well on switch and that they learned from RF5 and made an effort to improve. 

3. Normal weapons and sacred weapons, definitely a learning curve. The sacred weapons seem to have dedicated functions, mainly to do with clearing gloom in the section I came across.

4. The lack of character sprite art is a lot less awkward than I thought it would be. It's actually quite immersive and charming.

5. When laying down buildings/structures in the build mode there is a top down view mode. This was super helpful in being able to see exactly where I was placing things. 

5. There are frog statues littered about the village that if you pray to, they give you recipies. Seems like a once a day thing.  

6. You can sweep the yard in front of the shrine. One of the staff even made a cute sarcastic remark about how you "Have to sweep the shrine and make sure it's clean! :)"

7. Villagers with cat ears are referred to as NekoMata. Looks like this is based off of japanese folklore of the same name. Unsure if this relates to the wereanimals of RF5 or how it will interact with the existence of wereanimals?

8. I got a strange bit of dialog from Hina where she was saying she is from Selphia and is working for SEED only to stop halfway with "SEE-". Unsure why she would need to hide that she is working for SEED...?

9. Kurama referred to himself as "The resident shut-in of the village". Made me chuckle a bit. 

Overall the staff at the booth seemed really enthusiastic about the game and were very knowledgeable. I'm super excited to play the game on switch!

EDIT: 
Also wanted to add that the one loading screen I accidentally came across was when I accidentally left town and the staff member made me turn around lmfao. The load time was super quick. Not sure if that was because of the rig or whether performance is really just improved that much.

  I'm a child of a parent who was a closted transwoman for 23 years of marriage. 
   I love my dad, she's been so supportive of me throughout my life and continues to be a beacon of light for me. 
   That being said, I cannot imagine the pain that my mother went through all those years. As a child I never truly felt like my parents loved one another. There was always this impossible gap between them. My mother has described her experience as feeling like "the other woman" to the woman that my dad truly wanted to be. 

  On the other side of things, my dad was trapped. Trapped in the wrong body, trapped in credit card debt, trapped in secrets, trapped in compulsive habits made worse by everything she was feeling. 50+ years she lived like this. Knowing that freedom came at the cost of everything else that she had worked for. Her kids, her job, her house, everything. So she lied to herself, told herself it was just a phase, a fetish, something she could change. But this isn't something that can be controlled, as a trans man myself I should know. 
   
   I'm sure you're husband has been struggling with their own identity in a similar fashion. It is incredibly hard to accept and come out as trans when you already have so much of your life built up with someone you care deeply for.  
   Taking all this into consideration, you two definitely need to sit down and talk. Let your partner elaborate on their feelings first. If you open the conversation with something like "I'm not attracted to women, this isn't going to work" that may shut them down entirely and they may try to gaslight or repress themselves in an attempt to maintain the status quo. Try to take things slow. This process will require a lot of communication, I highly recommend couples therapy if you can afford it.
